maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.d: Return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.i: depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)). BFS counting levels also works.

maximum-product-subarray.d: Return the largest product of any contiguous subarray.
maximum-product-subarray.i: A negative number flips max and min, so track both the max and min product ending here. Equivalent trick: the best subarray is a prefix or a suffix between zeros, so scan prefix and suffix products, resetting to 1 after a zero.
k: Prefix and suffix products, reset at 0

maximum-score-after-splitting-a-string.d: Split a binary string into two non-empty parts. Score = zeros in the left + ones in the right. Return the maximum score.
maximum-score-after-splitting-a-string.i: Precompute suffix counts of ones (or start with the total ones and subtract as you go), then scan each split point once.
k: Suffix count of ones + one scan

maximum-subarray.d: Return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray.
maximum-subarray.i: Kadane's algorithm: keep a running sum, record the max, and reset the sum to 0 when it goes negative (a negative prefix only hurts).

median-of-two-sorted-arrays.d: Return the median of two sorted arrays in O(log(m+n)).
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.i: Binary search the partition in the smaller array: take i from nums1 and half - i from nums2. The partition is correct when l1 <= r2 and l2 <= r1; then the median comes from max(l1,l2) and min(r1,r2). Use +/- infinity at the edges.
k: Binary search on partition of smaller array

merge-intervals.i: Sort by start. If the current interval starts at or before the last merged interval's end, extend that end; otherwise start a new interval.
k: Sort by start + extend last merged

merge-k-sorted-lists.d: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
merge-k-sorted-lists.i: Min-heap of the k list heads: pop the smallest, append it, push its next node. Divide and conquer (merge lists in pairs) gives the same O(N log k).

merge-sorted-array.d: nums1 has m values followed by n empty slots; merge sorted nums2 into it in place.
merge-sorted-array.i: Fill from the back: compare the largest remaining of each array and write it at index m+n-1, moving backwards. No extra array needed.
k: Merge into a temporary list, copy back

merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.d: You can merge triplets by taking element-wise maximums. Can you produce exactly the target triplet?
merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet.i: Ignore any triplet with a value larger than the target in some position (it would overshoot). From the rest, check that each target coordinate is matched exactly by some triplet.
k: Filter overshooting triplets, collect matched indices

merge-two-sorted-lists.d: Merge two sorted linked lists by splicing their nodes.
merge-two-sorted-lists.i: Dummy head + tail pointer; attach the smaller head each step, then append whatever remains.

middle-of-the-linked-list.d: Return the middle node of a linked list (the second middle if there are two).
middle-of-the-linked-list.i: Slow/fast pointers: when fast reaches the end, slow is at the middle.

min-cost-climbing-stairs.d: Paying cost[i] lets you climb 1 or 2 steps from step i. Starting at step 0 or 1, return the minimum cost to reach the top (just past the last step).
min-cost-climbing-stairs.i: f(i) = min(f(i-1) + cost[i-1], f(i-2) + cost[i-2]) with f(0) = f(1) = 0.

min-cost-to-connect-all-points.d: Connect all points with the minimum total Manhattan-distance edge cost.
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.i: Minimum spanning tree. Prim's: start at any node, repeatedly take the cheapest edge to an unvisited node using a min-heap. Kruskal with union-find also works.

min-stack.d: Design a stack supporting push, pop, top and getMin, all in O(1).
min-stack.ex: push -2, push 0, push -3, getMin -> -3, pop, getMin -> -2
min-stack.i: Store each element together with the minimum of the stack at the time it was pushed; getMin reads the top's stored minimum.

minimum-changes-to-make-alternating-bina.d: Return the minimum number of bit flips to make a binary string alternate (no two adjacent equal).
minimum-changes-to-make-alternating-bina.i: Only two targets exist: 0101... and 1010.... Count mismatches against the first (x); the other needs n - x. Answer = min(x, n - x).

minimum-falling-path-sum.d: In an n x n matrix, a falling path picks one cell per row, moving down, down-left or down-right. Return the minimum path sum.
minimum-falling-path-sum.i: dp[i][j] = matrix[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j-1], dp[i-1][j], dp[i-1][j+1]). Keep only the previous row; the answer is the min of the last row.
k: Row-by-row DP with one previous row

minimum-insertion-steps-to-make-a-string.d: Return the minimum number of character insertions to make s a palindrome.
minimum-insertion-steps-to-make-a-string.i: Keep the longest palindromic subsequence and insert a partner for every other character: answer = n - LPS = n - LCS(s, reverse(s)).

minimum-number-of-pushes-to-type-word-i.d: Remap distinct letters onto keys 2-9 (any number per key). Typing the kth letter on a key costs k pushes. Minimise the total pushes to type a word with distinct letters.
minimum-number-of-pushes-to-type-word-i.i: 8 keys: the first 8 letters cost 1 push each, the next 8 cost 2, and so on. Answer = sum over i of (i / 8 + 1).
k: Greedy fill 8 keys per push level

minimum-path-sum.d: Moving only right or down, find the minimum-sum path from the top-left to the bottom-right of a grid.
minimum-path-sum.i: dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). One row of state is enough.

minimum-window-substring.d: Return the shortest substring of s containing every character of t (with multiplicity), or "".
minimum-window-substring.i: Variable sliding window with counts. 'have' = number of characters whose required count is met, 'need' = distinct characters in t. Expand right; while have == need, record the answer and shrink from the left.
